$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.check.common.design. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-DUP-CODE-BARE-RUN-OFF
arms.note: no run is bare any more, so a row of declarations and field fills whose values are names and literals is reported as a clone again under both readings, though nothing in it can be extracted

arms.name: M-DUP-CODE-NORM-KEY
arms.find: text: SpanRender.renderSpan(ctx.source, span.from, span.to, node, holes),
arms.note: statements compare on the whitespace-collapsed norm again, so two runs differing only inside a string literal bucket into one three-gram and are reported as a clone

arms.name: M-DUP-CODE-RENAMED-GATE-RAW
arms.note: the content gate measures each copy's own bytes again, binder names and hole markers included, so a run whose bytes are mostly long names passes on the anchor's spelling and is reported as a renamed clone

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-REPEAT-RENDER-SPLIT
arms.note: every norm bucket stays one group, so occurrences whose literals differ are still counted as one repeated expression and the message quotes a spelling the reported span does not carry

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-REPEAT-UNKNOWN-WRITE
arms.note: a write whose target no key names (`f().x = …`) is taken to write nothing instead of every operand

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-REPEAT-CLOSURE-WRITE
arms.note: a write inside a nested or sibling closure, which runs whenever that closure is called, no longer kills the group

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-REPEAT-REBIND
arms.note: occurrences whose operands bind different declarations (three comprehension binders) stay one group

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-REPEAT-TARGET-COUNTED
arms.note: a write target counts as an occurrence, so two reads of `a.b.c` and the assignment that replaces it are reported as three readings of one value

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-REPEAT-REFERENCE-READ
arms.note: a write BELOW a chain the group itself is (`a.b.c.d = …` under `a.b.c`) is taken to change the reference the chain holds

arms.name: M-GATE-TS-SINKS-BLIND
arms.note: thread-safety without sinks is reported as running

arms.name: M-GATE-TS-EXCLUDE-BLIND
arms.note: a thread-safety exclude path is reported as scanned

arms.name: M-TS-FIRST-FILE-LISTS
arms.note: every file is judged by the thread-safety lists of the chain the first file sits under

arms.name: M-ANON-FIRST-FILE-CONFIG
arms.note: every file is held to the thresholds of the chain the first file sits under

arms.name: M-ANON-ANCHOR-UNGATED
arms.note: a group anchored in a file that disables the rule is dropped for every file

arms.name: M-DUP-ANCHOR-UNGATED
arms.note: a clone whose later copy sits in a disabled file is reported nowhere

arms.name: M-TS-LONG-NEVER-GROWS
arms.note: a hold across a blocking call no longer makes its lock long, so the main-thread take of a lock a worker sleeps under goes unreported

arms.name: M-TS-HELD-ANY-THREAD
arms.note: a hold of a lock only background threads take is reported as a main-thread stall

arms.name: M-TS-EVIDENCE-UNCAPPED
arms.note: a hold's blocking calls past the cap vanish from its finding instead of being counted

arms.name: M-TS-HOLD-ANCHOR-LAST
arms.note: a hold's finding sits at its last blocking call, not where the stall first begins

arms.name: M-TS-UNKNOWN-LOCK-UNNAMED
arms.note: a hold of a lock no member names is reported naming nothing

arms.name: M-TS-QUIET-LOUD-CALLER
arms.note: a quiet root loud UI code also calls stays quiet, so everything it reaches from that handler goes unreported

arms.name: M-TS-QUIET-INTO-CALLBACK
arms.find: final loud: Int = ((ctx & CTX_QUIET) != 0 ? CTX_MAIN : 0) | (ctx & (CTX_MAIN | CTX_BG));
arms.note: a callback a quiet root registers or spawns inherits its quiet, so a listener or worker it hands on is never reported

arms.name: M-TS-ORDER-NO-HELPER-HOLDS
arms.note: a helper taking two locks leaves neither held in its caller, so a re-take under them reads as a new order

arms.name: M-TS-THROW-PER-TAKE
arms.note: two takes of one lock held at one throw are two findings

arms.name: M-TS-THROW-HELPER-HOLDS-UNREAD
arms.note: the holds a multi-lock helper opens in its caller never escape, so a throw under them is quiet

arms.name: M-TS-STORE-INERT
arms.note: a method assigned to a dynamic member runs where it is assigned, so a handler a worker invokes reads as run by the constructor that stored it

arms.name: M-TS-STORE-UNMIRRORED
arms.find: for (id in runs) for (e in graph.inEdges(id).copy()) if (e.kind != Contains) graph.deriveEdge({
arms.replace: for (id in runs) for (e in graph.inEdges(id).copy()) if (false) graph.deriveEdge({
arms.note: a value stored into a dynamic member is never called where the member is, so the chain to it names no invoker and its thread is a guess

arms.name: M-TS-STORE-SEALED-BLIND
arms.note: a call of the member's name the graph cannot resolve is taken to run nothing stored, so the value loses the context it may run in

arms.name: M-TS-NEVER-INVOKES-BY-TARGET
arms.note: a qualified neverInvokes entry is never matched, so removing a handler still reads as running it

arms.name: M-TS-NEVER-INVOKES-BY-NAME
arms.note: a bare neverInvokes name matches only a call the graph resolves, so removing a handler inherited from a library type still runs it

arms.name: M-TS-MAIN-CHECK-NO-GETTER
arms.find: matchAll(graph, mainChecks.concat([for (c in mainChecks) getterOf(c, accessorPrefixes)]))
arms.note: a main-thread check written as a property is never recognised at its reads, which call the getter

arms.name: M-TS-CLOSED-WORLD-UNREAD
arms.note: closedWorld is never read, so a method nothing calls is still assumed to run on the main thread

arms.name: M-TS-SEAL-CTOR
arms.note: a constructor nothing in the run constructs reads as dead, so the app's entry object runs on no thread

arms.name: M-TS-SEAL-OVERRIDE
arms.note: an override of a library method reads as dead, though the library calls it

arms.name: M-TS-SEAL-SUPERTYPE
arms.note: a method an unindexed interface may declare reads as dead, though code outside the run calls it through that interface

arms.name: M-TS-SEAL-UNRESOLVED
arms.note: a method an unresolved call may name reads as dead

arms.name: M-TS-DEAD-HOLDS-KEPT
arms.find: final acquires: Array<LockAcquire> = [for (a in sites.acquires) if (states.edgeContext(a.edge) != 0) a];
arms.note: a hold in a function no thread runs is reported, and makes its lock long

arms.name: M-IDIOM-GETTER-HOP
arms.note: a getter hop in a receiver path reads as a plain field, so a call that runs the getter once replaces writes that ran it once each

arms.name: M-IDIOM-NO-PURITY
arms.note: an impure right-hand side is carried into the call, where every argument is evaluated before any write

arms.name: M-IDIOM-NO-EARLIER-READ-GATE
arms.note: a right-hand side reading a field written above it reads the NEW value today and the old one in the call

arms.name: M-IDIOM-SUBTYPES-ALWAYS
arms.note: a subclass receiver matches without the opt-in, though its override of the method may not be the declared equivalence

arms.name: M-IDIOM-NO-COMMENT-GATE
arms.note: a comment between the writes, or trailing the last one, is deleted with them or left describing the whole call

arms.name: M-IDIOM-NO-SELF-TYPE-GATE
arms.find: if (host == null || ConfiguredTypes.inherits(ctx.index, host, idiom.type) != false) return null;
arms.note: the declared method's own body is rewritten into a call of itself, which recurses forever

arms.name: M-IDIOM-READER-LENIENT
arms.note: an idiom naming a field twice survives the reader, so a window writing one field twice is matched against a two-field method

arms.name: M-IDIOM-VALIDATE-TRUSTS
arms.note: a declared field that is a property with an accessor, or a static, is trusted as the plain field the equivalence needs

arms.name: M-EVENT-NO-MISMATCH
arms.note: a listener typed for another event class is not reported, and its constant is retyped into a compile error

arms.name: M-EVENT-ABSTRACT-TRUSTED
arms.note: an abstract without the String conversions is trusted, so every comparison or String use of a retyped constant stops compiling

arms.name: M-EVENT-NO-BASE-GATE
arms.note: a String constant of a class that is no event is retyped to an event type

arms.name: M-EVENT-NO-USE-GATE
arms.note: a constant no use names as an event type — none at all, or only the constructor of a class that is no event — is reported and retyped

arms.name: M-EVENT-STATIC-VAR
arms.note: a mutable static var is retyped as if it were a constant

arms.name: M-EVENT-ANY-NEW-IS-A-USE
arms.note: a string handed to the constructor of a class that is no event counts as a dispatch, and is reported as one of the wrong class

arms.name: M-TS-DATA-MEMBER-LAMBDA
arms.note: a finding in a lambda keys by the lambda's own id, which moves with every lambda written before it

arms.name: M-TS-ASIDE-KEEPS-SEEDS
arms.note: the counterfactual keeps the lock's own leak and blind reasons, so a lock long by a leak never shows what else holds it long

arms.name: M-TS-DATA-SUBJECT-UNSORTED
arms.note: a subject naming several ids keeps the graph's order, so one finding re-keys when the graph or the walk meets them another way

arms.name: M-TS-DATA-RAISER-CHAIN
arms.note: a throw raised by a callee keys with no chain, so the evidence of which call raises is lost to every tool

arms.name: M-TS-DATA-INIT-LAMBDA
arms.find: final container: Null<String> = graph.inEdges(cursor).find(e -> e.kind == Contains)?.from;
arms.note: a field initializer's lambda keys as the bare type, apart from the initializer's own calls

arms.name: M-TS-MAINSHORT-LOUD-ONLY
arms.note: a short lock a quiet root takes on the main thread is missing from the main-thread takes

arms.name: M-TS-UPWARD-INERT
arms.note: a value stored where it never runs from repeats with the loop that stores it

arms.name: M-TS-B-MAIN-ONLY-KEPT
arms.find: final mainOnly: Bool = lock != null && (states.edgeContext(a.edge) & CTX_BG) == 0
arms.note: a hold only the main thread runs is a stall like any other

arms.name: M-TS-B-ASSUMED-IGNORED
arms.note: a holder whose thread is only assumed main is taken for a main-only one

arms.name: M-TS-B-UNKNOWN-AS-MAIN-ONLY
arms.note: a hold of a lock no member names is judged by the holder's thread alone, as if no other could hold it

arms.name: M-TS-NEST-OFF
arms.note: a hold inside another hold of its function warns on its own

arms.name: M-TS-HELPER-CROSSING
arms.note: a helper twin's give makes its locks long as a crossing release

arms.name: M-TS-COVER-NOTE
arms.note: a closedWorld the run does not cover is read as false without a word

arms.name: M-TS-ENCLOSED-OFF
arms.note: a hold every caller's hold of its lock encloses warns on its own

arms.name: M-TS-UNNAMED-PAIR
arms.note: a hold of an unnamed lock warns though the main thread never takes its pair

arms.name: M-TS-NEST-HANDOFF
arms.note: a handed-off hold counts as an inner hold of the hold around its take, though it outlives that window

arms.name: M-TS-ENCLOSED-NOTE
arms.find: is long through the call into this one'
arms.note: the enclosed hold's note claims the enclosing finding names its calls, which it may not

arms.name: M-TS-COVER-PARSED
arms.note: a run file that fails to parse counts as covering its part of the project

arms.name: M-TS-OPT-SINKS-UNMATCHED
arms.note: a sinks list naming no call of the run reads as a working one

arms.name: M-TS-OPT-SKIP-DECLARED
arms.note: a chain with no usable sinks is not scanned, so what its config lost is never said

arms.name: M-TS-OPT-NO-SINK-NOTICES
arms.note: a run no sink matches returns before its config problems are said

arms.name: M-TS-QUIET-HOLD
arms.note: a hold only a quiet root runs reports as the main thread's own long work, though the root waits on purpose

arms.name: M-TS-BUILTIN-NEEDS-SINKS
arms.note: a chain writing no sinks of its own is no config to report on, so a malformed option of it goes unsaid

arms.name: M-TS-REPORT-NEEDS-SINKS
arms.note: the report gate wants sinks of the chain's own, so a chain writing other options only reports nothing though the builtin sinks apply

arms.name: M-TS-WAIVE-SINKS-WIN
arms.replace: final sinkIds: Array<String> = [for (id in configured) if (!waived.contains(id)) id];
arms.note: a nonBlocking entry waives a call the project's own sinks list

arms.name: M-TS-BUILTIN-NOTICE-OFF
arms.note: a run never says which builtin sinks it applied

arms.name: M-TS-LIB-NOT-SINKS
arms.note: a library call whose body blocks is no sink of the chain that walked it

arms.name: M-TS-ORDER-HANDED-ANYWHERE
arms.note: a value a spawns or registers call runs elsewhere is walked as if it ran under the hold

arms.name: M-TS-PAIR-OFF
arms.note: two holds one call of a multi-lock helper opens, across the same calls, warn twice

arms.name: M-TS-PAIR-ORDER
arms.note: either hold one helper call opens folds onto the other, whichever comes first, not the lock the helper takes first

arms.name: M-TS-FOLD-HELPER-CROSSING
arms.note: a multi-lock helper's give counts as a crossing release for the fold: a wait for its lock is never covered

arms.name: M-TS-NEST-SUPPRESSED
arms.note: a hold taken inside a hold whose warning a directive silences turns info onto it

arms.name: M-TS-ENCLOSED-SUPPRESSED
arms.note: a hold enclosed by a hold whose warning a directive silences turns info onto it

arms.name: M-TS-UNSEALED-NOTE
arms.note: a hold whose lock member a reflective write unsealed no longer says which member and which writers (review R3 M4)

arms.name: M-TS-UNSEALED-THROW
arms.note: a hold left on a throw whose lock member a reflective write unsealed no longer says who unsealed it

arms.name: M-TS-CTOR-STORE-INERT
arms.note: a value a constructor only stores runs where it is handed, under the hold around the `new` (R7 L1b, client ItemList.reload)

arms.name: M-OWNED-OWNERS-IGNORED
arms.note: no owner glob owns anything, so every mention inside a declared owner is reported

arms.name: M-OWNED-DECLARING-MODULE
arms.note: the module declaring an owned type is no owner of it, so its own declaration and body are reported

arms.name: M-OWNED-ENCLOSING-TYPE
arms.note: an owner naming a sub-type owns nothing, since only the module path is matched

arms.name: M-OWNED-FREE-REPORTED
arms.replace: case Free: { decls: [], outside: [], open: true };
arms.note: a name no resolution tier binds, which only a built-in can be, is reported as an unknown mention

arms.name: M-OWNED-UNKNOWN-SILENT
arms.note: a name a tier could bind to something the index does not hold reads as provably another type, and the reach goes unreported

arms.name: M-OWNED-BOUND-BY-NAME
arms.note: a name bound to a same-named type of another package is reported as the owned type

arms.name: M-OWNED-VALUE-IS-TYPE
arms.find: return TypeResolver.resolveBindingFrom(name, span, tree, scan.shape) != null;
arms.note: an identifier the scope binds to a value is read as the type it is named like

arms.name: M-OWNED-IMPORTS-IGNORED
arms.find: for (s in scan.subjects) if (s.member != null ? path == s.label : importNames(path, s, scan.index)) report(scan, s, imp.span);
arms.note: an import or an alias of an owned type is not a mention

arms.name: M-OWNED-ALIAS-IGNORED
arms.note: a type position spelling an owned type through an import alias is not seen

arms.name: M-OWNED-QUALIFIED-EXPR-IGNORED
arms.note: a qualified owned type in an expression (`pkg.T.make()`) is not a mention

arms.name: M-OWNED-CTOR-ANY-TYPE
arms.note: constructing a same-named type of another package is reported as constructing the owned one

arms.name: M-OWNED-INSTANCE-BY-NAME
arms.note: an instance member is matched by name on a receiver the typer cannot type

arms.name: M-OWNED-STATIC-UNKNOWN-SILENT
arms.find: return named != null && denotes(scan, named, subject);
arms.replace: return named != null && !named.open && denotes(scan, named, subject);
arms.note: a static reached through a receiver whose meaning is unknown goes unreported

arms.name: M-OWNED-NO-SUPERTYPE-WALK
arms.note: an owned instance member reached through a receiver of a subtype is not seen

arms.name: M-OWNED-STATIC-THROUGH-SUBTYPE
arms.note: a static reached through a subtype of its type is reported, a reach Haxe itself rejects (`Class<B> has no field`)

arms.name: M-OWNED-SKIP-REASON-NULL
arms.note: the rule claims every file of a config that declares no ownedTypes

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-GRANT-UNBOUNDED
arms.replace: final maxMembers: Int = grant == null ? cfg.maxMembers : 1000000;
arms.note: a grant silences its type's member count at any size again, the ceiling read and ignored

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-GRANT-LINES-UNBOUNDED
arms.replace: final maxLines: Int = grant == null ? cfg.maxLines : 1000000;
arms.note: a grant silences its type's line extent at any size, whether it gave a line ceiling or not

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-UNGRANTED-DIMENSION
arms.replace: final maxLines: Int = grant == null ? cfg.maxLines : grant.lines ?? 1000000;
arms.note: a members-only grant forgives the line extent too

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-BEYOND-UNNAMED
arms.note: a type past its grant's ceiling is reported without naming the grant it outgrew

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-PROBLEM-ONCE
arms.note: a refused grant is reported once per FILE resolving its config, not once per run

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-PROBLEM-SILENT
arms.note: a refused grant grants nothing but says nothing either

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-LEGACY-GRANT
arms.replace:
if (identifier.match(head)) return { name: head, members: 1000000, lines: 1000000, head: head };
		if (false) {
arms.note: a ceiling-less `Name: reason` grant is read as an unbounded grant again, silently

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-GRANT-REASONLESS
arms.note: a grant whose `:` is followed by no reason is accepted

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-GRANT-NAME
arms.note: a grant head naming no identifier (`C<T> <= …`) is accepted

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CLAUSE-ORDER
arms.note: a members ceiling written after the lines ceiling is accepted

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CLAUSE-REPEATED
arms.note: a second lines ceiling overwrites the first instead of refusing the grant

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CEILING-DIGITS
arms.note: a ceiling of ten or more digits is read, by a parseInt whose answer differs per target

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-DUPLICATE-GRANT
arms.note: two grants for one type both stand, and the first found wins

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CEILING-AT-THRESHOLD
arms.find: if (ceiling != null && ceiling <= (unit == 'members' ? maxMembers : maxLines)) grantsNothing = true;
arms.note: a ceiling at or below the rule's threshold is read as a tighter limit instead of being refused

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-COUNTED
arms.find: final names: Array<String> = [for (i => m in all) if (!constant[i]) m.node.name ?? ''];
arms.replace: final names: Array<String> = [for (i => m in all) m.node.name ?? ''];
arms.note: the constants count toward the member total again

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-LINES-COUNTED
arms.find: final lines: Int = extent - constantLines(source, span.from, all, constant);
arms.note: the lines of the constants count toward the line extent again

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-REGION-OWN-LINES
arms.find: final owned: Int = newlinesIn(source, previousEnd, span.to);
arms.replace: final owned: Int = newlinesIn(source, span.from, span.to) + 1;
arms.note: a constant owns only its own lines, so its doc comment and the blank lines above it count as behaviour

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-SHARED-LINE
arms.note: a line a constant shares with a behaviour member is dropped with the constant

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-NEEDS-STATIC
arms.note: an instance final of a literal is read as a constant

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-STATIC-VAR
arms.note: a static var (state) is read as a constant

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-INLINE-PROOF
arms.note: the inline modifier is no longer the compiler's proof, so an inline final the compiler folds from a call counts

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-ANY-STATIC-FINAL
arms.note: every static final with an initializer is a constant, a run-time call included

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-ACCESSOR
arms.note: a property of an enum abstract is read as an enum value

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-ANY-ENUM-HOST
arms.note: a non-static field of ANY type is read as an enum value

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-NO-ENUM-VALUES
arms.note: the values of an @:enum abstract count as members again

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-ENUM-VALUE-NEEDS-INIT
arms.note: an implicit enum value (no initializer) counts as a member

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-NAME-NOT-CONSTANT
arms.note: a reference to a non-constant member of the type is read as a constant one

arms.name: M-OVERSIZED-CONST-NAME-UNDECLARED
arms.note: a name the type does not declare (an import, an inherited or module-level symbol) is read as a constant

arms.name: M-TS-SPAWN-MAIN-CONTEXT
arms.note: a value at a main position takes the spawn's background context

arms.name: M-OWNED-TIER-NO-USE-SITE
arms.note: a simple name is resolved with no use site, so a #if-guarded import never decides a use inside its own branch and the receiver reads as unknown

arms.name: M-OWNED-MEMO-IGNORES-SITE
arms.note: a file holding a guarded import answers every use of a name as its first use did, whichever #if branch each sits in

arms.name: M-OWNED-CANDIDATES-IGNORED
arms.note: an Unknown name whose every candidate is read and none is owned is still reported, by the member name alone

arms.name: M-OWNED-OUTSIDE-CANDIDATE-IGNORED
arms.note: a candidate outside the index — a std type a guarded alias names — is never the owned type

arms.name: M-REFUSAL-ASSERT-BINDER-READ-IGNORED
arms.find: for (group in groups) if (CasePatternScan.mentionCount(seams, arm, group[0].name) > group.length) return null;
arms.note: a binder the arm reads no longer spares it, so a test that checks the refusal's message is reported as passing on any refusal

arms.name: M-REFUSAL-ASSERT-PASS-UNREQUIRED
arms.find: return body.exists(node -> callsAny(seams, node, options.passes)) ? ctor : null;
arms.note: an arm is reported whatever its body does, so the arm that FAILS on an unexpected refusal reads as a pass

arms.name: M-ZERO-FIXTURE-PARSE-IGNORED
arms.find: return text == null || ParseGate.parseOrNull(scan.plugin, text) != null;
arms.note: every fixture reads as unparseable, so a zero-count assertion over a well-formed file is reported

arms.name: M-ZERO-FIXTURE-WRAP-FOLLOWED
arms.find: if (parent.kind != seams.callKind || hops >= MAX_HOPS) return false;
arms.replace: if (parent.kind != seams.callKind || hops >= MAX_HOPS) return true;
arms.note: a value concatenated into the source on the way counts as the source itself, so a member snippet a helper wraps in a class reads as an unparseable fixture

arms.name: M-ZERO-FIXTURE-SKIP-IGNORED
arms.note: a declared skip-parse test is read like any other, so its deliberately unparseable fixture is reported

arms.name: M-GUARD-PIN-OWN-KILLER-COUNTED
arms.note: an arm the guard names as its own killer counts as a hidden one, so a declared kill is reported

arms.name: M-GUARD-PIN-TYPE-UNREAD
arms.note: a member name alone reaches an arm, so a guard calling a same-named member of another type is reported

arms.name: M-RCAST-MERGE-FAMILIES
arms.note: checked and unchecked casts of one operand and type share a bucket again, so two unchecked casts and a checked one are reported together although the checked one carries a runtime check

arms.name: M-RCAST-WRITE-NOT-SPLIT
arms.note: a write of the operand between two casts no longer ends the run, so the later cast is bound to the earlier value, and one whose right side holds the first cast reads the old one

arms.name: M-RCAST-BACK-EDGE
arms.note: a write a loop carries round to an earlier cast no longer drops the run, so a loop that advances the operand is bound to its first value and never ends

arms.name: M-RCAST-HOIST-ABOVE-GUARD
arms.note: the path from the hoist statement to the first cast is no longer required to run it first and always, so the local is placed above the guard that makes the checked cast valid

arms.name: M-RCAST-CONDITION-SLOT
arms.note: a branching statement counts through any child, so a cast in an unbraced then or else body is hoisted above the guard

arms.name: M-RCAST-PURE-PREFIX
arms.note: code ahead of the first cast in its statement is ignored, so the bind runs before a write or a call it used to run after, and two runs in one statement lose an insertion

arms.name: M-RCAST-OWN-DECLARATION
arms.note: the local goes ahead of the statement declaring its operand, so it casts an outer binding of that name, or fails to compile with none

arms.name: M-RCAST-CASE-GUARD
arms.note: a case arm's guard counts as a statement of its body, so the local is put ahead of the guard and the arm no longer parses

arms.name: M-RCAST-SHORT-CIRCUIT
arms.note: a short-circuit operator counts as evaluating every operand, so a cast its right side may never run is bound ahead of it and throws where it never did

arms.name: M-RCAST-CAPTURE-WRITTEN
arms.note: a function literal's cast joins the outer run though the function writes the operand later, so the literal reads the value the local bound before the write
